A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RQI research, despite the changed title and substantial revision. The complete main texts, tables, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GT-quality analyses, a user study covering 2,496 images, IQA benchmark evaluations and RQI ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original user-study and benchmark results and adds comparator evaluations, loss ablations and experiments training SR models with RQI.

M1.justification: v3 adds an SR-training procedure using the original objective plus an RQI term weighted by -0.1 (Section 5.4). Appendix E explains its integration into SwinIR, SeeSR and PiSA-SR, including image-space feedback through SeeSR's frozen decoder. The core asymmetric MOS-difference metric and IQA backbones remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds SRIQA-Bench evaluation and LSDIR training/validation for the new SR-optimization task. The original five SR benchmarks, three IQA training datasets and BSD-SR/QADS/Kadid-10K evaluations remain. Set5 and Set14 were already evaluated in v1, so their prominence in v3 is not new coverage.

E2.justification: AFINE and DeQA-Score are added to the existing user-study and public-benchmark metric comparisons. The new SR-training experiment compares original-loss, AFINE-assisted and RQI-assisted versions of SwinIR, SeeSR and PiSA-SR. The seven SR methods in the original user study remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces controlled SR retraining on LSDIR, with original-loss and AFINE-loss comparison arms, and testing on LSDIR/DIV2K using five quality metrics. Appendix E specifies staged training schedules. The original 2AFC study, scene-separated 80/20 IQA split and multiscale patch evaluation are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds L1/L2/Huber loss ablations and an AFINE failure case involving subtle quality differences. It removes v1's systematic GT-quality filtering analysis, including MANIQA-based filtering and random-discard controls, rather than relocating them. The same-distortion and single-scale ablations are retained as Table 5; StableSR/PASD behavior case studies are removed.

E5.justification: v3 supplementary Figure 5 identifies the retained user-score error bars as 95% confidence intervals. v1 Figure 7 already displays those bars but does not define them. Neither version supplies repeated-training-run counts, seeds or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds benchmark, comparator, SR-training and loss-ablation results while retaining the original user-study scores. DeQA-Score's added Set5/Set14 SRCC of 0.699 exceeds RQI's unchanged 0.664. Table 3 appears to interchange the earlier BSD-SR/QADS PLCC-mean and SRCC-all values, and changes QADS RQI PLCC-all from 0.822 to 0.832; these do not establish performance gains.

T1.justification: The stated training-pair domain changes from indices 0 through n in v1 Section 4 to 1 through n in v3 Section 4.1, excluding the pristine reference as written. v3 also formally defines the new SR-optimization objective in Equation 3. No theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on systematically demonstrating GT-quality bias and correcting it with RQI. v3 reframes the contributions around broader FR/NR evaluation challenges, emphasizes fine-grained discrimination and fidelity, and adds the substantive claim that RQI improves SR models when used for optimization.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting dense pairings and regression to fine-grained discrimination, and weaker SwinIR training gains to limited generative capacity. Appendix F newly restricts meaningful score comparisons to a shared reference and distinguishes perceptual texture quality from pixel-accurate fidelity. The cross-content restriction remains in tension with the retained across-content generalization discussion.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies Huber regression, exact test downsampling factors, SR-loss weighting, staged training budgets and model-specific integration details. It also adds a project website link, without establishing its contents in the PDFs. Existing IQA learning rates, batch sizes, crop sizes and validation splits are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises positioning around AFINE, distinguishing RQI's general training framework and use of existing IQA datasets from AFINE's SR-specific approach. It adds discussion of DeQA-Score, NeuralSBS, probability-based formulations and recent diffusion SR methods. The KonIQ++ citation and associated GT-analysis context disappear.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. User-study and metric analysis now precede and motivate RQI; the method receives separate training, evaluation and implementation subsections. Supplementary material is reorganized and consolidated after the references, with several earlier figure-reference errors resolved.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the RQI diagram, replaces the opening visual presentation, expands comparison tables, moves user-preference plots into the supplement and removes GT-quality distributions/filtering plots. It adds SR-training comparison figures and new experimental tables. Several qualitative panels are retained or recomposed rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: Comparisons with AFINE and DeQA-Score, SRIQA-Bench testing, loss ablations and controlled SR-training experiments strengthen evidence for RQI's relevance and practical utility. Clearer implementation and limitations also help. These gains are qualified by the apparent Table 3 row transpositions, removal of direct GT-quality controls and unresolved cross-content interpretation, supporting a limited overall improvement.
